frequency_question: How often do partisan federal election administration bills pass the U.S. Senate?
membership_rule: Stands for bills targeting federal voter registration requirements, franchise expansion, or restrictions that became major partisan centerpieces and reached Senate floor consideration or major cloture votes.

cases.name: Freedom to Vote Act / For the People Act cloture attempts
Freedom to Vote Act re-introduction push

coverage_note: 3 named; represents the distinct legislative vehicles of major electoral reform in the modern polarized Senate.
known_gaps: Minor technical amendments to HAVA are excluded; only major partisan reform centerpieces are counted.
skeleton: Major partisan election bills introduced and brought to a significant procedural test in the Senate during polarized eras (2000-2026).
multiplier: 1 hit out of 3 major distinct legislative push cycles where one party attempted to unilaterally pass sweeping election rules over filibuster constraints.
validity_reason: Valid until the expiration of the current congressional makeup and filibuster structure rules.
